title: Papoutsakia
subtitle: Stuffed aubergine halves with tomato sauce and bechamel
excerpt: Hollowed aubergine halves filled with spiced tomato sauce, then topped with a thick bechamel and baked until golden. A Greek taverna classic that eats like a complete meal.
sourceNotes: Greek papoutsakia tradition, meaning little shoes. Vegetarian adaptation uses the scooped aubergine flesh in the filling.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Fill the aubergine halves up to a day ahead and refrigerate. Add the bechamel just before baking.

content.text: Papoutsakia means little shoes in Greek, named for the shape of the stuffed aubergine. The scooped flesh goes into the filling so nothing is wasted. Keep the bechamel thick so it sits on top and forms a golden cap.

Heat the oven to 190C. Score the cut faces of the aubergine halves in a crosshatch pattern, cutting 1cm deep but not through the skin. Brush with 3 tablespoons of olive oil and season. Place cut-side down on a baking tray and roast for 20 minutes until soft.
Turn the aubergines cut-side up and leave to cool slightly. Use a spoon to scoop out most of the flesh, leaving a 1cm shell. Roughly chop the scooped flesh.

Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, cinnamon, and oregano and stir for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree and tinned tomatoes. Stir in the chopped aubergine flesh. Simmer for 10 minutes until thick. Season well.

Make the bechamel. Melt the butter in a small saucepan over a medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in the warm milk until smooth and thick. Stir in half the parmesan and the nutmeg. Season.
Sit the hollowed aubergine halves in a roasting tin. Spoon the tomato filling into each shell. Top each one with a generous spoonful of bechamel. Scatter over the remaining parmesan.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the tops are deep gold. Rest for 10 minutes before serving. They hold their shape better once slightly cooled.

items.cause: Too much flesh was scooped out, leaving the walls too thin.
items.fix: Leave at least a 1cm layer of flesh all the way around the inside of the skin.

items.cause: The tomato sauce was not reduced enough before filling.
items.fix: Cook the filling until it holds its shape when pressed with the back of a spoon before spooning into the shells.

items.cause: The topping was uneven, or the oven has hot spots.
items.fix: Smooth the bechamel flat with a wet spoon before baking and rotate the tin halfway through.
